A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of IPDreamer with matching methods and experiments. The supplied v2 ends after its references; v3 includes Appendices A–E, which are assessed as newly supplied content.

before.justification: v2 reports original generated 3D objects, qualitative baseline comparisons, and geometry and texture ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation experiments and adds quantitative comparisons, a user study, quantitative ablation results, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The NeRF-to-mesh pipeline, IPSD geometry and texture optimization, geometry prompt difference, and main Equations (1)–(10) are retained. Combining IPSD with Zero-1-to-3 for single-image generation was already described in v2 Section 4.4; v3 supplies further documentation rather than establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The same text-to-3D, image-guided editing, and single-image-to-3D tasks remain. v3 modestly extends tested input conditions through deliberately extreme reference/coarse-object mismatches in Figure 5 and the failed doll example in Figure D. Complex-image guidance itself was already demonstrated in v2.

E2.justification: DreamFusion, Magic3D, Fantasia3D, and ProlificDreamer remain the text-to-3D baselines; Zero-1-to-3 and SyncDreamer remain single-image comparators. v3 additionally evaluates Zero-1-to-3 against IPDreamer in the text-to-3D comparison of Section 4.4/Figure 7, where v2 showed IPDreamer examples without that comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds FID against Stable Diffusion images and text-image CLIP evaluation over 20 prompts. It introduces an 80-volunteer, 16-prompt, 1,280-pair preference study with image prompts generated without scribble guidance, plus image-image CLIP evaluation of the geometry prompt difference. These substantially expand v2's visual evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: The visual geometry-prompt-difference ablation in v2 Figure 8 is replaced by an aggregate alignment ablation in v3 Table 3, while the normal-map ablation is retained. v3 also adds a stagewise optimization example, a joint-loss comparison in Figure C, and a failed style-transfer case in Figure D, substantially expanding component and failure analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v3's new scores and preference percentages remain point estimates; its volunteer and comparison counts describe evaluation sample sizes rather than repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: v3 adds numerical results absent from v2: IPDreamer obtains FID 257.17 and CLIP score 0.2859 in Table 1, 58.35% preference against ProlificDreamer in Table 2, and image-alignment scores of 0.8228 without versus 0.8389 with the geometry prompt difference in Table 3. Additional qualitative comparisons and failure outcomes also appear. These are newly reported results, not measured improvements over v2.

T1.justification: Main Equations (1)–(10) remain unchanged. Appendix C adds explicit decoupled-attention and weighted joint IPSD/Zero-1-to-3 gradient definitions in Equations (A.1)–(A.4), providing a limited expansion of the mathematical specification without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central IPSD, appearance-control, and high-quality generation claims remain. v3 extends the stated applicability to guidance by arbitrary complex images and makes limitations of existing single-image-to-3D methods an explicit central motivation, broadening v2's predominantly text-to-3D framing.

C2.justification: v2 stresses dependence on initial NeRF quality and warns that IPSD alone cannot fully preserve reference identity. v3 instead emphasizes that a basic coarse NeRF suffices and presents IPSD as improving existing single-image methods, omitting that explicit identity warning. Appendix D newly documents hours-long optimization and incomplete style control, supported by the failure in Figure D.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link and substantial implementation documentation in Appendix C: A100 hardware, 5k/10k/15k optimization steps, timestep schedules, batch size 1, rendering resolution 512, memory requirements, and attention/joint-loss details. It also supplies a prompt list. These are newly disclosed settings, not evidence that retained experiments changed their training budgets.

R1.justification: v3 adds InstantID, SSR-Encoder, ConsistNet, and references supporting CLIP evaluation, FID, and optimization. Most related-work discussion remains intact, with additional positioning around image-prompt adaptation and existing single-image methods' difficulty handling complex images.

P1.justification: Selected passages in the abstract, introduction, method overview, NeRF discussion, and conclusion are rewritten around complex-image guidance. Experimental subsections are reorganized and 'embeddings' often becomes 'features'. The main section hierarchy and much of the related-work and technical exposition remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The two-column layout becomes single-column, the pipeline illustration is simplified, and several figure panels are substantially rearranged, including v2 Figure 3 becoming v3 Figure 4. New quantitative tables and appendix displays expand the presentation. Portions of v2 Figure 4 reappear in v3 Figure 7 and Figure B rather than being wholly removed.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens v2's qualitative-only validation through quantitative baseline comparisons, human preferences, and an aggregate ablation, while providing essential training details and explicit failure limitations. These additions address important evidential and reproducibility gaps. Reporting remains imperfect: Table 2's Fantasia3D percentages sum to 98%, and Table A lists 20 prompts under a user-study caption although Section 4.3 specifies 16. These inconsistencies limit confidence but do not outweigh the substantial gains in support and documentation.
